## What changed or decided
Three behaviors, confined to the 5 declared locks:

1. **Install stamp** (`scripts/shiki_installer.py`) — every install/upgrade writes `.shiki/install-stamp.json`: platform commit, install timestamp, and a per-path SHA-256 over the **platform-owned (overwrite-category) shipped files** (project-content/governance/preserve-outright are excluded so per-target customization isn't false drift). It's **untracked local state**; the installer idempotently ensures the target's `.gitignore` ignores it — because a tracked unknown `.shiki/` path fails `validate_shiki` and the loop's `git add -A` would otherwise commit it into a permanently-red Validate check. A no-op re-install leaves the stamp byte-identical; a proven-older lineage never overwrites a newer one.
2. **Doctor drift** (`scripts/shiki_doctor.py`) — three new findings with their own ids: `doctor.install_stamp.present` (absent → `warn`, distinct, never a pass), `.content` (hand-edit/half-upgrade → `warn`, names the exact drifted paths), `.platform_commit` (stamp not an ancestor of the running platform HEAD → `warn`). All `warn`/`skip`, so `--strict` fails on them; doctor never writes to the target.
3. **Migrate `--target` fix** (`scripts/shiki_migrations.py`) — `cmd_migrate` **refuses** when `--target` names a repository whose own `scripts/shiki_migrations.py` **differs** (byte-compare) from the running platform's, with a message naming the correct command (`cd <target> && … migrate <cmd>`). A freshly installed target (identical registry) and `--target == platform root` are allowed, so the safer-default refusal never fires spuriously.
